A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VERINA, with the same 189 Lean problems and three foundational tasks. Text, equations, figures, tables, and all appendices are readable and support comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original LLM evaluations, proof-refinement experiments, specification-evaluator validation, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds end-to-end evaluations, contamination analysis, sensitivity experiments, and proof-cost and failure analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 4 revise the end-to-end workflow: ProofGen receives the generated specification in v2 but the ground-truth specification in v3, preventing trivially equivalent generated code and specifications. This changes one workflow's inputs; the foundational modules and specification-evaluation pipeline otherwise remain.

E1.justification: The 189 Lean problems and their sources remain unchanged. V3 adds actual evaluation requiring jointly correct code, specifications, and proofs in the end-to-end setting, previously described without corresponding joint results. Appendix B additionally uses The Stack as a contamination-audit corpus. No evaluation in Dafny or Verus is added.

E2.justification: V3 expands the general-purpose comparison from eight to ten models by evaluating o3 and Claude Opus 4.0 across foundational and contextual conditions. In the specialized-prover comparison, o3 replaces GPT 4.1 in v2 Figure 6 versus v3 Figure 7, although GPT 4.1 remains evaluated elsewhere. Human proofs also become an explicit proof-length comparator.

E3.justification: V3 introduces joint Code&Spec and End-to-End scoring with the revised ground-truth proof target. New experimental protocols include varying property-based testing budgets from 10 to 2,000, replacing code references with behavioral summaries, and comparing refinement with COPRA under matched token budgets. Existing generation temperatures, token limits, and prompt blocks are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds testing-budget sensitivity, code-summary ablations, contamination-overlap analysis, human-versus-generated proof-length analysis, token-normalized COPRA comparisons, and categorized proof failures. These investigate evaluator stability, contextual information, efficiency, and failure mechanisms. The earlier proof-versus-testing validation and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: V3 Table 6 adds averages over five property-based-testing seeds and standard deviations for Unknown percentages. V2 already reports five generated responses per problem and bounds derived from unknown evaluation outcomes. The addition does not establish an increase in the foundational generation sample counts.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports o3 at 72.6%, 52.3%, and 4.9% for code, specification, and proof generation; the previous o4-mini entries remain 61.4%, 51.0%, and 3.6%. New joint results peak at 41.2% for Code&Spec and 3.2% end-to-end. DeepSeek Prover V2 7B's reported pass@1 changes from 11.1% in v2 Figure 6 to 8.6% in v3 Figure 7. Numerous diagnostic and ablation results are also added.

T1.justification: The four formal soundness/completeness conditions in Section 4.1 and their appendix explanations remain unchanged. The Lean evaluation examples and case-study proofs are retained. No new theorem, formal assumption, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a manually curated, modular Lean benchmark, a proof-and-testing specification evaluator, and evidence that proof generation is the principal bottleneck. Updated leading-model scores and additional experiments change the supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations concerning summary failures, proof verbosity, library knowledge, and diminishing returns from inference budgets, plus limitations on extending to Dafny and Verus. Appendices A–B newly argue transfer across verification paradigms and elimination of direct and indirect contamination risks. These are substantially stronger interpretations than v2's contamination-risk acknowledgment and exceed what the reported tests establish.

D1.justification: Table 3 adds checkpoint identifiers, pricing, and costs for o3 and Claude Opus 4.0. Section 3.2 documents manual Lean coverage checks and separate pre/post-condition negative-test categories; Appendix C.3 explains the specialized prompt choice through parsing failures. Core prompts, hardware, generation settings, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands Lean's research positioning through production applications such as Cedar, LNSym, Clear, and CSLib, and arguments connecting ITP findings to ATP systems. Additional literature supports cross-language testing and contamination analysis. Existing benchmark comparisons remain; publication updates and the duplicate differential-privacy reference do not represent new research works.

P1.justification: The main section order and most existing prose remain intact. V3 makes localized explanatory and grammatical edits, adds acknowledgments and conference headers, and inserts extended-discussion appendices before the existing material. Original prompts and case studies are unchanged apart from numbering, so this is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: V3 redraws the evaluator and workflow diagrams, expands model-comparison displays, and adds end-to-end, proof-length, and token-budget plots. New tables present sensitivity, summary ablations, subset breakdowns, and proof-failure categories. Existing refinement curves are retained, while several figures and tables are relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical support by measuring the previously unreported joint workflow and adding seed/budget checks, cost comparisons, and systematic failure analyses. These improve benchmarking and diagnosis. The gains are tempered by the ground-truth-assisted meaning of end-to-end proof generation and by claims eliminating contamination or ensuring transfer beyond Lean that exceed the reported evidence.
